description:
FILED s473t5a (#1501 CHECK 1 round 2, 2026-09-13).

`perl-tests/t/test.pl:123-126` is:

    # run_multiple_progs - skip
    sub run_multiple_progs {
        # Skip - runs multiple Perl scripts
    }

perl's own `t/test.pl` implements it: it reads a `__DATA__`/`\*DATA` stream of
`PROGRAM ... EXPECT ... ########` records, runs each program in a child perl
and compares the child's combined output with the EXPECT text, one TAP row per
record.  A file whose whole body is `run_multiple_progs('', \*DATA)` therefore
reports `1..0` under PCL.

MEASURED (this extraction, `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1`), the five
companion files that call it and what they cost:

    file            perl    PCL     rows short (row-shortfall.tsv)
    t/op/tie.t      94/1    0/0     95
    t/op/fork.t     28/0    1/0     27
    t/op/runlevel.t 24/0    0/0     24
    t/op/anonsub.t  14/1    1/5     9
    t/io/data.t      4/0    0/0      4
                                   ---
                                   159

t/op/tie.t is the biggest single item in the s473t5a population and the only
one of the five in the 50-199 band; the other four are in the 1-49 bands and
belong to later rounds by size, but they are ONE cause.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE -- the #1590 CLIFF.  Implementing it means ~40 more
lines in `perl-tests/t/test.pl`, and #1590 measured that ~26 extra lines in
that file tip `t/re/pat_advanced.t` over SBCL's default 1 GB dynamic space
(`SB-REGALLOC::PACK-TN`, 97.9 % allocated) and cost that file ALL 1680 of its
rows.  So this task is blocked on the same unblock as #1590: a per-call
`--dynamic-space-size` in `tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm`, or the Target-B question of
why a 296 KB emission needs a gigabyte to compile.  Do NOT add the helper
before that; measure re/pat_advanced.t in the same change if you do.

WHAT THE HELPER NEEDS FROM PCL (all of it exists): a DATA filehandle (the stub
already supports `\*DATA`), a child perl (`_pcl_child_perl` -- since #348 the
children are PCL via `tools/pclperl-for-tests`), and `$^X`-style switch
handling.  perl's version also honours per-record `# SKIP`, `# TODO` and
`# NAME` directives and a `PROG`/`EXPECT` split on `/^########/m` -- the
directives are what makes a faithful port bigger than the obvious loop.  A
partial port that ignores them would manufacture failures, not rows.


=== DONE (s484d, shipped; bars re-measured s486c on the rebased tree) ===

`run_multiple_progs` was a NO-OP in the PCL test.pl stub, so a file whose whole
body is `run_multiple_progs('', \*DATA)` planned `1..0` and its rows simply did
not exist.  Implemented on the stub's EXISTING child mechanism (`run_perl`
through $ENV{PCLPERL}, so the child is PCL -- #348), never a second one;
`run_perl` gains perl's own `progfile` argument.  Measured `--jobs 1`, each
mover's #366 serial re-run agreeing, against a `git archive f6b56feb`
extraction:

  op/tie.t        0/0  -> 14/81  (95 rows, perl 95)
  op/fork.t       1/0  -> 20/8   (28 rows, perl 28)
  op/runlevel.t   0/0  -> 8/16   (24 rows, perl 24)
  op/anonsub.t    1/5  -> 6/9    (15 rows, perl 15)
  io/data.t       0/0  -> 3/1    (4 rows, perl 4)

= 159 rows produced, +50 passing, and all five files' row-shortfall entries go
to ZERO.  It also moves the perl-tests SWEEP: anonsub.t 1/0 -> 6/4, TOTAL
18676 -> 18681, both baselines edited row by row.

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM PERL, both measured, both commented at the site: the
failure diagnostic is ALWAYS commented (this runner captures `> out 2>&1`, so
the raw form injected two phantom TAP rows), and it is commented perl's
`_comment()` way rather than `s/^/# /mg` -- because **PCL's `^` under /m also
matches after a FINAL trailing newline** (filed #1766), which appended a stray
`# ` that glued itself to the next TAP row and lost 81 of op/tie.t's 95.

Residue filed with causes in the row baseline: op/tie.t 81 (66 = #155),
op/runlevel.t 16 (#1769), op/fork.t 8 (#1770), op/anonsub.t 9 (#1771; four are
principle 9), io/data.t 1 (#1767).

BARS on the combined tree (s486c, rebased onto main 4429126a): gate
`Result: PASS` 243 files / 8216 rows; full perl-tests sweep GATE clean,
0 new / 0 fixed, TOTAL passing 18681 = 18681 (+0), drops 5 = census.
Companion `--all --quick --jobs 2`: see the s486c record.
subject: The PCL test.pl stub's `run_multiple_progs` is a NO-OP -- five companion files (t/op/tie.t 95, op/fork.t 27, op/runlevel.t 24, op/anonsub.t 9, io/data.t 4 = 159 rows) produce almost nothing; BLOCKED on #1590's heap headroom
